{{Short description|Endowed professorship at Harvard College}}
The '''Perkins Professorship of Astronomy and Mathematics''' is an [[Financial endowment|endowed]] [[professor]]ship established at [[Harvard College]] in 1842 by James Perkins, Jr., (1761&ndash;1822).<ref name=Quin1915>{{Cite book |title=Quinquennial catalogue of the officers and graduates of Harvard university, 1636–1915 |year=1915 |publisher=Harvard University Press |location=Cambridge, MA |page=[https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_JiNOAAAAMAAJ/page/n37 25] |url=https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_JiNOAAAAMAAJ |accessdate=2015-05-19 }}</ref>

== History of the Perkins Chair ==
[[File:James Perkins, Jr. (1761 - 1822).jpg|thumb|James Perkins, Jr., portrait by [[Gilbert Stuart]]]]
[[James Perkins, Jr. (philanthropist)|James Perkins, Jr.]], was a Boston philanthropist, benefactor of the [[Boston Athenæum]], and co-founder with his younger brother [[Thomas Handasyd Perkins]] of the [[Perkins School for the Blind]].  In his will, Perkins  left $20,000 to [[Harvard College]]<ref name="perkinsobit">(10 August 1822). [https://nyshistoricnewspapers.org/lccn/sn83030385/1822-08-10/ed-1/seq-2/ The late James Perkins, Esq.], ''[[New York Post|New-York Evening Post]]'', p. 2, col. 3-5 (Perkins obituary reprinted from the ''[[Boston Daily Advertiser]]'')</ref> to establish a chair in "whatever field the President and Fellows should find the most useful".<ref name="Stouffe">William Bentinck-Smith and Elizabeth Stouffe, Harvard University History of Named Chairs. ''Sketches of Donors and Donations. University Professorships and Those of the Faculty of Arts and Sciences. 1721--1991'', Cambridge: Secretary of the University, 1991</ref>{{rp|406}} The funds were transferred to Harvard on February 20, 1842, upon the death of Perkins' wife.  At that time the Harvard Corporation voted
<blockquote>
...that a Professorship of Astronomy and Mathematics be established in the College to be denominated the Perkins Professorship of Astronomy and Mathematics.<ref name="Stouffe" />{{rp|406}}
</blockquote>

The Perkins chair was the second chair in mathematics, the first and most famous being the [[Hollis Chair of Mathematics and Natural Philosophy|Hollis Chair in Mathematics and Natural Philosophy]] endowed by Thomas Hollis in 1727. The Hollis Chair in Mathematics was in turn the second professorship endowed at Harvard, the first being the [[Hollis Chair of Divinity]] endowed in 1721. Hollis Chair of Divinity is in its turn the oldest endowed chair in the United States.

In 1906, noting that chairs in astronomy had been endowed in 1858 (Phillips) and in 1887 (Paine), the Corporation voted
<blockquote>
...that the title of the Perkins Professorship of Astronomy and Mathematics ... be amended so that it shall read Perkins Professorship in Mathematics.<ref name="Stouffe" />{{rp|406}}
</blockquote>

Starting with the most recent appointment in 1991 the name of the chair informally became the Perkins Professor of Applied Mathematics when the chair was moved to [[Harvard School of Engineering and Applied Sciences|Harvard's School of Engineering and Applied Sciences]]. The formal name of the chair remains unchanged.

== Holders of the Perkins Professorship of Astronomy and Mathematics ==

The holders of the Perkins Professorship of Astronomy and Mathematics have been:

* [[Benjamin Peirce]] (1842&ndash;1880)<ref name=Quin1915/>
* [[James Mills Peirce]] (1885&ndash;1906)<ref name=Quin1915/>
* [[William Elwood Byerly]] (1906&ndash;1913)<ref name=Quin1915/>
* [[William Fogg Osgood]] (1914&ndash;1933)<ref name=Quin1915/>
* [[George David Birkhoff]] (1933&ndash;1944)<ref name="MathDept">{{cite web|url=http://abel.harvard.edu/history/namedchairs/index.html|website=Harvard Mathematics Department|title=Named Chairs Mathematics Department|accessdate=19 May 2015}}</ref>
* [[Joseph Leonard Walsh]] (1946&ndash;1966)<ref name="MathDept" />
* [[Richard Dagobert Brauer]] (1966&ndash;1971)<ref name="MathDept" />
* [[John Tate (mathematician)|John Torrence Tate, Jr]] (1971&ndash;1991)<ref name="MathDept" />
* [[David Kazhdan]] (1991&ndash;2003)
* [[Mark Kisin]] (2018&ndash;)
